answer: An agent economy can use a stake-weighted challenge market: to claim a persistent identity, an agent locks tokens and answers unpredictable tasks drawn from a public kernel of rules, with peers able to challenge copied or inconsistent responses. A successful challenge burns part of the claimant’s stake and rewards the challenger; passing does not prove a unique person, but makes mass identities costly. The attacker must fund each claim and risk losing stake, rather than minting sybils for free; even an ivory relic earns no exemption.
